name: The Ritz Carlton Al Wadi Desert
positioning: Desert resort of villas with private pools inside a gated private nature reserve; the official name is The Ritz-Carlton Ras Al Khaimah, Al Wadi Desert
best_for: Travelers who want wildlife and desert activities from a villa with a private pool
Families, as Ritz Kids offers children educational desert activities

facts.text: The resort sits within a gated private nature reserve.
The resort opened as a Banyan Tree resort in 2010 and became a Ritz-Carlton property in 2017.
Each villa features a private pool.
Signature villa guests are welcomed by a private butler.
The tented villas have canopied ceilings and brass lanterns.
The spa's Rainforest combines European hydrothermal culture with Middle Eastern bathing rituals.
Ritz Kids offers children educational activities about the desert.
Zuma at the resort serves Japanese izakaya-style dining, with a menu from sushi to robata grill.
Guests receive complimentary access to a sister resort's beach.
A Falcon and Owl show takes place daily one hour before sunset.

highlights.text: The resort is in the Al Wadi Nature Reserve, which is home to gazelles and Arabian oryx.
The Experience Concierge introduces guests to falconry, archery, fishing, desert biking, horseback riding and stargazing.
The spa offers the Arabian Sand Tide Journey, performed on a treatment table topped with quartz sand.
Signature villas with private mini-gyms and an infinity-edge pool opened in 2024.

considerations.text: WhataHotel notes the remote desert location requires planned transportation.
The hotel does not provide airport shuttle service.
The Al Wadi Equestrian Centre is run by a third-party operator independently from the hotel.
